newsitem.title: USA: Alyeska schedules steps to stop vibrations.
newsitem.headline: Alyeska schedules steps to stop vibrations.

text.p: A new valve will be installed in the trans-Alaska pipeline to to stop vibrations that have rattled residents at the bottom of a steep mountain pass, the company's president said Friday.

Bob Malone, president of Alyeska Pipeline Service Co, said the vibrations resulted from decreased oil flow through the 800 mile line, and the resulting "free-fall" effect as oil tumbles through some vacant space down 2,000-foot Thompson Pass north of Valdez.

Pipeline flow peaked in 1988 at over two million barrels a day. But since then, production from the supergiant but maturing Prudhoe Bay field has steadily declined. Despite new oil from other fields, North Slope production is now about 1.3 million to 1.4 million barrels a day, Malone said.
Alyeska is a consortium owned by oil companies with interests on Alaska's North Slope.
British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield and Exxon together own 90 percent of Alyeska. Mobil, Unocal, Amerada Hess and Phillips Petroleum own minor shares.
